title: Blood DNA methylation in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC): a prospective cohort study.
authors: Balnis, Joseph; Madrid, Andy; Drake, Lisa A; Vancavage, Rachel; Tiwari, Anupama; Patel, Vraj J; Ramos, Ramon Bossardi; Schwarz, John J; Yucel, Recai; Singer, Harold A; Alisch, Reid S; Jaitovich, Ariel
one_liner_zh: 该前瞻性队列研究分析PASC患者外周血DNA甲基化与症状关联，虽用机器学习分类严重度并涉及转录因子基序，但核心是表观遗传临床关联，无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: DNA methylation integrates environmental signals with transcriptional programs. COVID-19 infection induces changes in the host methylome. While post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) is a long-term complication of acute illness, its association with DNA methylation is unknown. No universal blood marker of PASC, superseding single organ dysfunctions, has yet been identified. METHODS: In this single centre prospective cohort study, PASC, post-COVID without PASC, and healthy participants were enrolled to investigate their symptoms association with peripheral blood DNA methylation data generated with state-of-the-art whole genome sequencing. PASC-induced quality-of-life deterioration was scored with a validated instrument, SF-36. Analyses were conducted to identify potential functional roles of differentially methylated loci, and machine learning algorithms were used to resolve PASC severity. FINDINGS: 103 patients with PASC (22.3% male, 77.7% female), 15 patients with previous COVID-19 infection but no PASC (40.0% male, 60.0% female), and 27 healthy volunteers (48.1% male, 51.9% female) were enrolled. Whole genome methylation sequencing revealed 39 differentially methylated regions (DMRs) specific to PASC, each harbouring an average of 15 consecutive positions, that differentiate patients with PASC from the two control groups. Motif analyses of PASC-regulated DMRs identify binding domains for transcription factors regulating circadian rhythm and others. Some DMRs annotated to protein coding genes were associated with changes of RNA expression. Machine learning support vector algorithm and random forest hierarchical clustering reveal 28 unique differentially methylated positions (DMPs) in the genome discriminating patients with better and worse quality of life. INTERPRETATION: Blood DNA methylation levels identify PASC, stratify PASC severity, and suggest that DNA motifs are targeted by circadian rhythm-regulating pathways in PASC. FUNDING: This project has been funded by the following agencies: NIH-AI173035 (A. Jaitovich and R. Alisch); and NIH-AG066179 (R. Alisch).
abstract_zh: 背景：DNA甲基化将环境信号与转录程序整合在一起。COVID-19感染会诱导宿主甲基化组发生变化。虽然COVID-19后急性后遗症（PASC）是急性疾病的长期并发症，但其与DNA甲基化的关联尚不清楚。目前尚未发现超越单一器官功能障碍的PASC通用血液标志物。方法：在这项单中心前瞻性队列研究中，纳入了PASC患者、无PASC的COVID-19后患者以及健康参与者，以研究其症状与外周血DNA甲基化数据（通过最先进的全基因组测序生成）之间的关联。PASC引起的生命质量恶化使用验证工具SF-36进行评分。分析旨在识别差异甲基化位点的潜在功能作用，并采用机器学习算法来解析PASC严重程度。结果：共纳入103名PASC患者（男性22.3%，女性77.7%）、15名既往感染COVID-19但无PASC的患者（男性40.0%，女性60.0%）以及27名健康志愿者（男性48.1%，女性51.9%）。全基因组甲基化测序揭示了39个PASC特异的差异甲基化区域（DMRs），每个区域平均包含15个连续位点，可将PASC患者与两个对照组区分开来。PASC调控的DMRs基序分析识别出调控昼夜节律及其他功能的转录因子结合域。一些注释到蛋白质编码基因的DMRs与RNA表达变化相关。机器学习支持向量算法和随机森林层次聚类揭示了基因组中28个独特的差异甲基化位点（DMPs），可区分生命质量较好和较差的患者。解释：血液DNA甲基化水平可识别PASC，对PASC严重程度进行分层，并提示在PASC中DNA基序受昼夜节律调控通路靶向。资金：本项目由以下机构资助：NIH-AI173035（A. Jaitovich和R. Alisch）；以及NIH-AG066179（R. Alisch）。
